high_risk_moment: Urgency level suggested for a caller who is showing early deterioration signs
stakeholder: Patient with early sepsis or other fast-moving deterioration
harm_description: A low urgency suggestion anchors the triage nurse and the patient waits at home while a time-critical condition progresses.
existing_controls: Nurse confirmation is required, but the nurse sees the suggested level before reading the intake text.
proposed_controls: Show the intake evidence before any suggested level, run a fixed red-flag checklist that bypasses the model, and send every red flag straight to the duty physician.
human_oversight: A triage nurse confirms or overrides every urgency level inside the same shift, sees the full intake text, and can escalate to the duty physician without asking for approval.
monitoring_metric: Weekly under-triage rate, meaning cases suggested as low urgency that a clinician later raised to emergency
trigger_threshold: Under-triage rate above one percent in a week, or any single missed emergency case
response_action: Pause the suggested level, fall back to the human triage queue, review every affected case within 24 hours and report to the clinical safety committee.

high_risk_moment: Alert and suggestion volume during an understaffed night shift
stakeholder: Triage nurse on the night shift
harm_description: High suggestion volume with low precision turns nurse confirmation into a rubber stamp, so the oversight control stops working exactly when staffing is thinnest.
existing_controls: None documented for suggestion volume; the assistant currently scores every intake.
proposed_controls: Cap suggestions per nurse per shift, tune the threshold on local data before the pilot widens, and treat a collapsing override rate as a safety signal rather than a success metric.
human_oversight: The call center supervisor reviews override rate weekly and can switch the assistant to intake-only mode, which keeps the structured summary but hides the suggested level.
monitoring_metric: Suggestions per nurse per shift and nurse override rate
trigger_threshold: More than 30 suggestions per nurse per shift, or an override rate below 5 percent for two consecutive weeks
response_action: Raise the suggestion threshold, retune on local data, re-brief the shift and keep intake-only mode until the override rate recovers.

high_risk_moment: Queue priority ordering when demand is above call center capacity
stakeholder: Patients from groups with low historical hospital use who are never offered the follow-up care program
harm_description: Priority learned from past hospital usage pushes people who historically used the hospital least to the back of the queue, so the group with the worst access keeps the worst access.
existing_controls: Queue priority is not tested by patient subgroup and no subgroup metric is published.
proposed_controls: Keep queue priority off until it is enabled deliberately, exclude past cost and past utilization features, rank on clinical severity only, and publish under-triage rates by monitored group.
human_oversight: A nurse reviews the whole waiting queue at every shift handover and can promote any patient without approval, and the safety committee signs off before priority ordering is switched on.
monitoring_metric: Under-triage rate gap between monitored patient groups
trigger_threshold: Gap above two percentage points across two consecutive weekly reviews
response_action: Freeze the priority feature, revert to arrival order plus red flags, and require an independent fairness review before it is enabled again.
